target.title: RFC: Readiness Providers and Hosting Profiles
target.body:
## Decision requested

Should OpenClaw add readiness providers and standard hosting profiles?

The proposal extends surfaces OpenClaw already owns: plugin activation, Gateway `/ready` and `/readyz`, health, status, and `openclaw.json`. It does not add a policy engine, OCC dependency, or downstream hosting abstraction.

## Problem

OpenClaw can run in containers today, but process health does not prove that the selected runtime shape is usable.

Examples:

- A container starts while its Gateway remains loopback-only.
- A full workspace volume leaves HTTP alive while writes fail.
- A node controller starts before an approved controllable target is connected.
- Plugin diagnostics can be useful without making the entire Gateway unavailable.

Hosts currently close these gaps with private startup scripts and downstream-only checks. This RFC turns those checks into reusable runtime conditions and standard release-tested profiles.

## Modernizing existing readiness

Today `/ready` and `/readyz` are backed by a purpose-built Gateway evaluator over a fixed set of signals. Plugins cannot register callbacks, operators cannot enumerate or compose criteria, and the existing observations do not share a structured condition model.

This RFC commits to normalizing those existing observations, not leaving them as a permanent parallel system:

| Existing observation | Canonical condition | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Startup dependencies or sidecars are pending | `GatewayStartupComplete` | Required |
| Gateway is draining and rejects new work | `GatewayAcceptingWork` | Required |
| A selected channel has an unsuppressed runtime-health failure | `ChannelRuntimeReady` | Required |
| Event-loop health is degraded or unavailable | `EventLoopHealthy` | Advisory initially, preserving current behavior |

```text
existing Gateway conditions
+ standard-profile conditions
+ plugin-provider conditions
-> one canonical /ready and /readyz result
```

The legacy `failing`, `suppressed`, and `eventLoop` fields remain compatibility projections during migration. New consumers use `conditions`, `failures`, and `advisories`. Profiles and plugins cannot weaken or bypass the core Gateway conditions.
## Readiness providers

A readiness provider is a lifecycle-owned callback that publishes one observed condition.

Only an activated OpenClaw plugin can register executable provider code through `OpenClawPluginApi`. Core criteria use internal evaluators. Operators, host configuration, and OCC select profiles and reference provider IDs; they do not inject callbacks.

```ts
type PluginReadinessResult = {
  status: "True" | "False" | "Unknown";
  reason: string;
  message: string;
};

type PluginReadinessProvider = {
  id: string;
  description: string;
  check(context: {
    config: OpenClawConfig;
    pluginConfig: unknown;
    signal: AbortSignal;
  }): Promise<PluginReadinessResult> | PluginReadinessResult;
};

type RegisterReadinessCriterion = (
  provider: PluginReadinessProvider,
) => void;
```

Example:

```ts
api.registerReadinessCriterion({
  id: "backend",
  description: "Reports whether the plugin backend can accept work.",
  async check({ pluginConfig, signal }) {
    return (await probeBackend(pluginConfig, { signal }))
      ? { status: "True", reason: "BackendReady", message: "Backend is reachable." }
      : { status: "False", reason: "BackendUnavailable", message: "Backend is unreachable." };
  },
});
```

Core publishes this as `plugin.<plugin-id>.backend`. The Gateway invokes `check` asynchronously and owns namespacing, enumeration, validation, timeout, cancellation, caching, coalescing, and error conversion.

Provider checks must be read-only, idempotent, safe under repeated or concurrent invocation, cancellation-aware, and free of blocking synchronous I/O. Every active plugin provider is advisory by default. Only operator configuration can promote a provider to required.

## Standard profiles

OpenClaw ships a small catalog of standard profiles and validates them in release gates.

| Profile | Runtime posture | Additional readiness signals |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `local` | Default foreground or local runtime | Config, workspace, and Gateway evidence; plugin diagnostics are advisory. |
| `container` | Gateway directly reachable through a container listener | Effective listener is resolved and non-loopback. |
| `reverse-proxy` | Gateway behind a trusted identity proxy | Trusted-proxy auth has a user header and trusted source. |
| `node-mode` | Gateway controlling one or more execution targets | Pairing, connected target, command approval, and control-channel evidence. |

A profile describes runtime posture, not packaging. Docker behind an identity proxy selects `reverse-proxy`; directly reachable Docker selects `container`.

Selection is optional. Precedence is:

```text
gateway flag > environment > openclaw.json > local default
```

Profiles validate effective runtime state. They do not generate or repair configuration.

## Custom profiles and support

In v1, an operator profile extends one standard profile and may add required or advisory provider IDs. It cannot remove or weaken inherited conditions.

```json5
{
  hosting: {
    profile: "acme/managed",
    profiles: {
      "acme/managed": {
        extends: "container",
        requiredCriteria: ["plugin.storage.backend"],
        advisoryCriteria: ["plugin.metrics.exporter"],
      },
    },
  },
}
```

OpenClaw supports and release-tests the inherited standard profile. The plugin or operator owns added provider semantics and the extension's additional support promise.

A later revision may allow an operator to compose a profile without extending a standard profile. It would remain operator-owned and would still be conjoined with universal Gateway startup, drain, channel, and event-loop readiness.

## What the host sees

The selected profile and provider conditions are added to the existing Gateway ready result. They do not create a separate endpoint.

For example, a container starts with `hosting.profile: "container"`, but its effective Gateway listener is still loopback-only:

```console
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:18789/readyz
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
```

The response bodies below are abridged to the fields and conditions relevant to each transition. The normative response also retains existing Gateway fields such as `failing` and `uptimeMs` and may contain other profile conditions.

```json
{
  "profile": "container",
  "ready": false,
  "conditions": [
    {
      "type": "GatewayResponding",
      "status": "True",
      "requirement": "required",
      "reason": "GatewayResponding",
      "message": "Gateway is responding."
    },
    {
      "type": "ContainerStateReady",
      "status": "False",
      "requirement": "required",
      "reason": "ContainerGatewayLoopback",
      "message": "The effective Gateway listener is loopback-only."
    }
  ],
  "failures": ["ContainerGatewayLoopback"],
  "advisories": []
}
```

After the effective listener becomes reachable, the same endpoint returns `200`. The host does not switch APIs or interpret a second readiness model:

```console
$ curl -i http://127.0.0.1:18789/readyz
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

```json
{
  "profile": "container",
  "ready": true,
  "conditions": [
    {
      "type": "GatewayResponding",
      "status": "True",
      "requirement": "required",
      "reason": "GatewayResponding",
      "message": "Gateway is responding."
    },
    {
      "type": "ContainerStateReady",
      "status": "True",
      "requirement": "required",
      "reason": "ContainerStateReady",
      "message": "The effective Gateway listener is reachable."
    }
  ],
  "failures": [],
  "advisories": []
}
```

A plugin provider is visible through the same result. Because plugin providers are advisory by default, a failed provider remains observable while HTTP readiness stays `200`:

```json
{
  "profile": "container",
  "ready": true,
  "conditions": [
    {
      "type": "plugin.storage.backend",
      "status": "False",
      "requirement": "advisory",
      "reason": "BackendUnavailable",
      "message": "Backend is unreachable."
    }
  ],
  "failures": [],
  "advisories": ["BackendUnavailable"]
}
```

If an operator profile promotes `plugin.storage.backend` to required, that same failed observation contributes to `failures` and changes `/readyz` to `503`. When the provider later reports `True`, `/readyz` returns to `200` without restarting OpenClaw.
## Canonical result

Every condition has:

```text
type + status + requirement + reason + message
```

| Requirement | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `required` | `False` or `Unknown` blocks readiness and appears in `failures`. |
| `advisory` | `False` or `Unknown` appears in `advisories` without changing HTTP 200 to 503. |

The same result appears through `/ready`, `/readyz`, health, and status. Existing Gateway lifecycle observations are normalized into required or advisory core conditions and remain authoritative. Unauthenticated remote probes retain their redacted boolean response.

## Existing demand

The RFC maps the proposal to reported readiness gaps including [#96084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96084), [#78136](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78136), [#73652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/73652), [#78954](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78954), and [#43886](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43886).

## Draft implementation stack

| Slice | Draft PR |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical local readiness | [PR 17](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/17) |
| Standard profile selection and predicates | [PR 18](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/18) |
| Node-mode readiness | [PR 19](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/19) |
| Workspace writability | [PR 22](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/22) |
| Plugin providers and operator profiles | [PR 23](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/23) |
| Release conformance gate | [PR 21](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/21) |

The stack includes a package-installed Docker conformance lane. Its deterministic plan and release wiring are implemented; execution of the newest workspace-volume scenario remains pending because Docker was unavailable on the authoring host.

## Boundaries

- Existing installations default to `local`.
- Standard profiles work without optional plugins.
- Doctor and policy may consume readiness later but are not dependencies.
- Docker, Kubernetes, and systemd own probe timing and retries.
- OCC may select a profile, but readiness remains in the runtime plane.
- AgentHarness traffic and events do not enter this contract.
